87: Kino is the main character of Kino's Journey. They are a composed, stoic, and precocious teenager who travels with their motorrad, Hermes, in search of a country with specific desired characteristics. Their gender is ambiguous.
88: Hermes is a talking motorrad who travels with Kino to various countries and lands. Hermes was found broken in an alley by the original Kino during his stay in the Land of Adults.
3872: The original Kino was a young man who traveled by the same three-day rule that the main character, Kino, does. His arrival in Land of Adults sparks the beginning of the story, and is Kino's inspiration to travel after they attempt to discover his past.
13970: Shizu is a young man with a great talent for swordsmanship, weilding a katana. He travels in a buggy alongside his vassal and pet Samoyed, Riku, and eventually Ti, a girl whom Riku and Shizu eventually take in.
15428: Riku is the pet dog of Shizu, and his loyal vassal. Despite being a dog, he is able to speak. He first appears alongside Shizu in the Land of Colosseum. He refers to his master as Master Shizu at all times.
15429: Sakura is a girl from the country Kino visited in the last episode of the anime series. She shares many similarities to Kino, such as her parents also owning an inn.
57697: Shishou is a former traveler who traveled the world several years ago before settling down in a forest near the Land of Adults. She is considered both scoundrel and savior as she is hailed a hero in some countries and a wanted fugitive in others.
150047: Tifana, better known as Ti (ティー), is one of two companions of Shizu during his travels. Riku serves as her guardian. Ti first introduced to Shizu in the Ship Country by an elder as his guide.
205872: Photo is a photographer and works with her partner, Sou - her red motorrad. Prior to this, she was a slave. Before becoming a slave, Photo was an orphan due to an epidemic sweeping in her country.
205873: Sou is a red motorrad and the partner of Photo, a photographer. He's is styled after the Honda Motocompo.
